questions.question: A regional tourism board has approved a program that will change how the organization operates and delivers value to visitors, with cloud services as the enabler. In the kickoff briefing, the program director wants to name this organizational change precisely for the board. Which term names it?

options.A: A hybrid cloud deployment
options.B: Digital transformation
options.C: The cloud
options.D: A modernized infrastructure estate

rationale.correct: Digital transformation is the organizational change itself: new ways of operating and delivering value that cloud and infrastructure make possible. The term covers the change program, not the technology underneath it.

distractors.A: A hybrid cloud deployment is one way to consume cloud services; naming a deployment model does not name the organizational change the board approved.
distractors.C: The cloud is the consumption model that enables the change, delivering technology on demand as services. It is the enabler, not the change in how the board operates.
distractors.D: Infrastructure is the underlying capability being modernized; it is one ingredient of the program, not the organizational change the director needs to name.

questions.question: A ceramics manufacturer pilots two AI tools. The first answers a question about a glaze defect and stops. The second is given the goal of clearing a production backlog: it checks kiln schedules, drafts a revised firing plan, reserves maintenance windows, and confirms the outcome. What makes the second tool agentic AI?

options.A: It was trained on a much larger dataset than the first tool
options.B: It generates novel content rather than analyzing existing records
options.C: It runs on infrastructure purpose-built for AI workloads
options.D: It pursues a goal through multiple steps and actions

rationale.correct: Agentic AI is defined by behavior: the system pursues a goal through multiple steps and actions, deciding what to do next until the goal is met. A single model call that answers and stops, however capable, is not agentic.

distractors.A: Training data volume says nothing about agency; a model trained on more data can still only answer once and stop.
distractors.B: Producing novel content describes generative AI. A generative model that drafts one plan and stops is still a single call, not goal pursuit.
distractors.C: Where a tool runs is an infrastructure fact. It may be true of either tool and does not distinguish goal-directed, multi-step behavior.

questions.question: A credit union is negotiating with a core-banking software vendor. Its technology committee has one firm requirement: the credit union must be able to inspect the code it will depend on, and modify it if the vendor's roadmap stalls. Which commitment should it ask the vendor to make?

options.A: Ship the product as open source software
options.B: Build the product on an open standard
options.C: Support deployment across multiple cloud providers
options.D: Publish integration APIs for the product

rationale.correct: Open source is the commitment that matches the requirement: the code is inspectable and modifiable, so the committee can read what it depends on and change it if the vendor stalls. An open standard is a different commitment, a shared specification anyone may implement.

distractors.B: An open standard is a shared specification anyone may implement. It protects interoperability between implementations, but it does not let the credit union inspect or modify the vendor's own code.
distractors.C: Multicloud portability is a real safeguard against provider lock-in, but it answers where the product runs, not whether its code can be inspected and modified.
distractors.D: Published APIs open the integration layer only; they expose none of the product's internals, so the committee still could not read or change the code.

questions.question: A cinema chain's online ticketing site fails every time tickets for a major release go on sale, because its servers are sized for a quiet weekday. The digital director is drafting the cloud business case and wants to lead with the property that most directly relieves this pain. Which framing should lead?

options.A: Cost-effectiveness: the chain pays only for resources it actually uses
options.B: Agility: new customer-facing features ship more frequently
options.C: Scalability: capacity grows with each on-sale peak and shrinks after it
options.D: Permanent capacity provisioned for the largest anticipated on-sale peak

rationale.correct: The stated pain is capacity pressure: demand spikes overwhelm servers sized for a quiet weekday. Scalability is the cloud property that answers capacity pressure, expanding with each peak and contracting afterward so the failure mode disappears.

distractors.A: Cost-effectiveness is a true cloud benefit, but it answers a question about spend structure. The site is failing on capacity, not on cost.
distractors.B: Agility and speed answer slow change: shipping features faster would not keep the ticketing site up during an on-sale peak.
distractors.D: Provisioning permanently for the largest peak throws fixed capacity at an elastic problem: it sits idle on quiet days and still fails when a bigger release breaks the estimate.

questions.question: A national postal service runs its parcel-tracking portal from a single data center in the capital. Customers tracking parcels from abroad see slow page loads, and one outage took the portal down for a full day. The board asks what a cloud provider's global footprint would buy beyond more machines. What is the accurate answer?

options.A: Serving users everywhere while staying up through failures
options.B: More total compute capacity than the current data center offers
options.C: Offsite backups that restore the portal after an outage
options.D: Lower infrastructure cost through pay-as-you-go pricing

rationale.correct: Global reach and high availability are what the footprint buys: services positioned near users everywhere, and continuity through failures because no single facility is a single point of failure. Neither outcome is about raw capacity.

distractors.B: Raw capacity is exactly what the board was told to look past: more machines in one capital data center would neither speed up access from abroad nor survive that facility failing.
distractors.C: Backups shorten recovery after an outage; they do not keep the portal serving during one, and they move nothing closer to customers abroad.
distractors.D: Pay-as-you-go pricing is a real benefit with a different address: it answers cost structure, not reach or availability.

questions.question: A garden centre chain's CFO has framed the cloud business case entirely as cheaper servers and more seasonal capacity. The CIO wants the case to also name benefits that are not about cost or capacity at all. Select the TWO benefits that belong in that addition.

options.A: A security baseline stronger than the chain can operate on its own
options.B: Near-unlimited capacity for the spring rush without buying hardware
options.C: Insights drawn from the sales and stock data the chain already holds
options.D: Paying only for the resources each store actually consumes
options.E: A provider that takes over the chain's regulatory compliance obligations

rationale.correct: Enhanced security and data-driven insights are the benefits that are not about cost or capacity: a provider-operated security baseline exceeding what the chain could run alone, and analysis that turns existing data into decisions. Together with strategic value and focus, they widen a case the CFO had reduced to servers and spend.

distractors.B: Elastic seasonal capacity is a genuine cloud benefit, but it is precisely the capacity story the CIO was asked to look beyond.
distractors.D: Consumption-based pricing is cost-effectiveness, the other axis the addition must avoid: it strengthens the spend argument, not the beyond-cost one.
distractors.E: No provider takes over a customer's compliance obligations; responsibility is shared, so this overstates what any cloud purchase delivers.

keywords: factors that motivate organizations to transform
questions.question: A wine importer and distributor is debating whether to launch a transformation program. Four reasons are raised in the leadership meeting. Which one is the kind of factor that genuinely motivates organizations to transform?

options.A: A high-profile generative AI launch suggests the newest platforms are the best ones
options.B: Managed cloud services have recently become available in the importer's region
options.C: The IT budget is showing an unspent balance as the fiscal year closes
options.D: A competitor now confirms restaurant orders in half the importer's turnaround time

rationale.correct: The factors that motivate organizations to transform are competitive, customer and market pressures, and a rival serving customers measurably better is exactly such a driver. Technology availability and internal budget positions describe means and timing, not the pressure that justifies the change.

distractors.A: A vendor launch is news about technology, and newest is not a business reason; without a competitive or customer pressure attached it motivates nothing.
distractors.B: Regional availability of managed services is true and useful, but it is an enabler: it explains how a program could run, not why the business needs one.
distractors.C: An unspent budget is an internal accounting fact. Spending it is not a transformation driver, and programs justified that way stall when the balance is gone.

keywords: common hurdles that can affect transformation
questions.question: A municipal fire service moved its incident-reporting system to the cloud a year ago. The platform performs well in every test, yet crews still file paper reports and station officers have quietly stopped chasing them. The program has stalled. Which hurdle does this describe?

options.A: The platform cannot handle peak incident volume
options.B: A skills and culture hurdle: crews were never brought along
options.C: The service selected the wrong cloud deployment model
options.D: Too little of the annual budget was reserved for software licensing

rationale.correct: This is one of the common hurdles that can affect transformation: the technology works, but adoption failed because skills, habits and ownership on the ground were never addressed. Transformation programs stall on people and culture at least as often as on platforms.

distractors.A: The evidence rules this out: the platform performs well in every test. Blaming capacity contradicts the stall as described.
distractors.C: Nothing in the stall points at where the system is deployed; crews avoiding a working tool is the same problem under any deployment model.
distractors.D: No licensing shortfall is described, and buying more licenses would not make crews use the system they already have.

keywords: implications and risks of not adopting cloud
questions.question: A campus bookstore chain has declined a proposed cloud program for the third year running, and its board minutes record the decision as prudent cost avoidance. Meanwhile its online competitors keep widening their lead in delivery speed and personalization each term. What is the chain actually accepting by standing still?

options.A: A compounding competitive disadvantage that grows harder to close each year
options.B: Only a delay: the same benefits will be available at the same cost later
options.C: A genuine reduction in overall technology spending
options.D: The retraining effort that cloud adoption would have required

rationale.correct: The implications and risks of not adopting cloud are stated as risk, not savings: while the chain stands still, competitors improve faster every cycle, so the gap compounds and the eventual catch-up costs more than the avoided program. Declining to move is a decision with a price.

distractors.B: Deferral is not neutral: each year of standing still adds competitor gains and legacy drift, so the same move later closes a wider gap at a higher price.
distractors.C: The savings are not real reductions: the aging estate still consumes maintenance and refresh spending while buying no competitive ground.
distractors.D: Retraining is a cost of adopting, not of declining; naming it here answers the wrong side of the decision.

questions.question: A physiotherapy clinic chain is choosing a strategic cloud partner for a data and AI roadmap. The board's stated concern is specific: years of appointment and outcome records must become usable for AI without rebuilding the data estate. Which of Google's claimed differentiators answers that concern?

options.A: World-leading AI models
options.B: AI Hypercomputer
options.C: An AI-ready data platform
options.D: The prestige of partnering with a recognized AI leader

rationale.correct: The concern is about the data estate, and the AI-ready data platform is the differentiator that answers it: the claim that existing data becomes usable for AI where it already lives, without a rebuild. Matching the differentiator to the question the stakeholder actually raised is the judgment this decision needs.

distractors.A: World-leading AI is a real claim answering a different question: model capability does nothing for records that are not yet usable as AI input.
distractors.B: AI Hypercomputer is the infrastructure-scale sibling on the same list; it answers training and serving horsepower, not whether the chain's records are AI-ready.
distractors.D: Prestige is not a differentiator or a decision criterion; a partner's brand answers no question about the chain's data estate.

questions.question: A radio broadcasting network must keep its broadcast playout systems in its own facilities under the terms of its transmission license, while its listener analytics should run on a public cloud's elastic capacity. The network wants both managed as one estate. Which deployment model is this?

options.A: Multicloud
options.B: Hybrid cloud
options.C: Private cloud for the whole estate
options.D: Public cloud with data residency settings for the playout systems

rationale.correct: A hybrid cloud combines an organization's own facilities with public cloud capacity under central management, which is exactly the described split: license-pinned playout on premises, elastic analytics in the public cloud, one estate.

distractors.A: Multicloud means deliberately using more than one public cloud provider; the scenario combines one provider with the network's own facilities, which is a different model.
distractors.C: Keeping everything private satisfies the license and surrenders the elastic analytics capacity the network wanted; it answers half the requirement.
distractors.D: Residency settings choose where data sits inside the provider's estate; the license requires the network's own facilities, which no provider-side setting delivers.

questions.question: A motorway toll operator is moving its customer portal to the cloud, and its program lead must explain to executives what happens when a driver types the portal's web address. Which explanation is correct at the level a leader needs?

options.A: The domain name is the numeric identifier, and the IP address is the readable name drivers type
options.B: Available bandwidth determines which server receives the request
options.C: A firewall translates the typed name into a network route
options.D: DNS resolves the typed name to the IP address that identifies the right server

rationale.correct: The purpose-level reading is that the domain name service (DNS) resolves the human-readable name into an IP address, and the IP address identifies the server that should receive the traffic. Name resolution and addressing are the two primitives a non-engineer still needs to keep straight.

distractors.A: This swaps the two terms: the IP address is the numeric identifier and the domain name is the readable form, not the reverse.
distractors.B: Bandwidth is how much data can move at once; it moves traffic, it does not decide where a typed name points.
distractors.C: A firewall permits or blocks traffic; turning names into addresses is name resolution, a different job at a different layer.

questions.question: An artisan food cooperative's member portal feels sluggish: every individual page click takes a noticeable moment to respond, yet the co-op's large nightly catalog uploads always finish quickly. Which network property does the complaint implicate?

options.A: Latency: how long one round trip takes
options.B: Bandwidth: how much data can move at once
options.C: Storage capacity on the portal's database server
options.D: The choice between public and private deployment

rationale.correct: Slow individual interactions alongside fast bulk transfers is the signature of a latency problem: each round trip takes too long, while bandwidth is clearly ample because large uploads finish quickly. The two properties answer different questions, and this complaint names the round-trip one.

distractors.B: Bandwidth is the property the evidence clears: nightly uploads moving large volumes quickly show the pipe is wide enough.
distractors.C: Storage capacity governs how much can be kept, not how long a page click waits; the described symptom is a network property.
distractors.D: Deployment model is not implicated by the evidence; a private estate with the same round-trip time would feel exactly as sluggish.

questions.question: A heavy-equipment leasing firm is drafting an internal briefing on where its fleet-telemetry workloads will physically run on Google Cloud. Which statement should the briefing use, because it describes Google's geography correctly?

options.A: Zones are collections of regions, so choosing a zone spreads workloads across several regions
options.B: Availability districts sit between regions and zones as an intermediate tier
options.C: Regions are collections of zones, and edge locations bring content closer to users
options.D: A region is one data center building, so which zone is selected makes no practical difference

rationale.correct: The tiers nest one way: regions are collections of zones, zones are the deployment areas within a region, and edge locations extend the network to bring content closer to users. Getting the nesting right is what makes placement and resilience discussions meaningful.

distractors.A: This inverts the hierarchy: a zone sits inside a region, so choosing one zone concentrates a workload rather than spreading it across regions.
distractors.B: No such tier exists in Google's geography; the plausible-sounding name does not correspond to anything the briefing could rely on.
distractors.D: A region is not a single building, and zone selection is exactly what separates workloads from shared failure; the claim erases the tier that matters.

questions.question: A public library system is classifying three shortlisted platforms for its new catalog service. For one of them, the provider provisions the servers and patches the operating system and runtime, while the library controls only its catalog application and its data. Which service model is that platform?

options.A: Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS)
options.B: Platform as a Service (PaaS)
options.C: Software as a Service (SaaS)
options.D: Serverless computing

rationale.correct: Service models are read from the responsibility boundary. When the provider operates the servers, operating system and runtime while the customer keeps the application and data, that boundary is Platform as a Service (PaaS): control of the application retained, operational burden below it traded away.

distractors.A: Under Infrastructure as a Service (IaaS) the library would be patching the operating system itself; the described boundary places that burden with the provider.
distractors.C: Under Software as a Service (SaaS) the library would consume a finished application; here it still builds and controls its own catalog application.
distractors.D: Serverless is a compute abstraction, not one of the service models being classified; it answers how code runs, not who is responsible for which layer.

questions.question: A bus and coach operator has fitted every vehicle with a position beacon and every conductor with a ticket scanner. Today, when a motorway closure splits a route, the control room only learns how badly the diverted services were overcrowded from the following morning's report. The operations director wants the same data to reach controllers while the disruption is still running. Which business value of data is that initiative pursuing?

options.A: Identifying trends, so each season's timetable reflects where demand has moved
options.B: Timelier reporting, from running the same overnight report on an hourly cycle
options.C: Generating real-time business insights, so controllers can act during the disruption
options.D: Fueling AI, once enough incident history exists to train a disruption model

rationale.correct: Generating real-time business insights is the value at stake: the data has to inform a decision while the disruption is still running, and an answer that arrives the following morning has already lost its worth. Identifying trends, informing strategic decision making and fueling AI are the other values this data can deliver, each answering a different question.

distractors.A: Identifying trends is a genuine value of the same data, and it shapes future timetables over a season; it does nothing for a control room deciding what to do while services are still diverted.
distractors.B: An hourly rerun of an overnight report is fresher and still a snapshot: between runs the control room is reading history, which is the shape of answer the director is trying to replace.
distractors.D: Fueling AI is a real value of accumulated incident data, and it postpones what the controllers need during this disruption until a model exists that nobody has trained yet.

questions.question: An environmental testing laboratory holds three kinds of evidence for every job: instrument readings in fixed columns, sensor logs that gain new fields whenever firmware changes, and scanned chain-of-custody forms. Most of the volume is the readings, and the lab's analysts already query them with SQL. Accreditation requires that the scans and the raw instrument traces be retained exactly as produced. Which storage archetype should hold all three?

options.A: A data lake, which holds structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in native form
options.B: A data warehouse, which organizes the evidence into a defined schema for analysis
options.C: A data warehouse for the readings, with the scans left on the existing file share
options.D: A data governance process that assigns an owner to each of the three kinds of evidence

rationale.correct: The discriminator is the shape of the data, not its volume. A data lake takes structured, semi-structured and unstructured data in native form, which is exactly what fixed-column readings, evolving sensor logs and scanned forms are together, and native form is what the accreditation rule demands.

distractors.B: A data warehouse is built for structured data under a defined schema, so the scanned forms and the evolving sensor logs would have to be reshaped or excluded, and reshaping is what accreditation forbids.
distractors.C: Warehousing the readings and leaving the scans on a file share serves the analysts' half of the problem and leaves the evidence accreditation cares about outside the storage decision entirely.
distractors.D: Assigning an owner to each kind of evidence is real data governance work, and it answers who may do what with the data rather than which archetype can hold all three.

questions.question: A commercial real estate developer buys a footfall dataset from a company that compiles anonymized movement counts from many retailers and mobile apps, none of which the developer has any relationship with. The developer pays a license fee and may use the counts freely in its site appraisals. How should this dataset be classified in the developer's data register?

options.A: Second-party data, shared directly by the organization that collected it
options.B: Third-party data, acquired from an aggregator that collected none of it itself
options.C: Brokered data, a separate class for information resold by an intermediary
options.D: First-party data, because the license fee transfers ownership to the developer

rationale.correct: Origin is what classifies data, not price or license terms. Third-party data is acquired from an external aggregator that collected it from neither the developer's own customers nor a named partner, which is why its coverage and accuracy have to be taken on the supplier's word.

distractors.A: Second-party data comes directly from a partner the organization deals with, and the developer deals with none of the retailers or apps behind these counts.
distractors.C: No such class exists in the first-party, second-party and third-party scheme, and resale through an intermediary is precisely what makes data third-party.
distractors.D: Paying for data does not change where it came from. A license grants use, while first-party data is data the developer collected itself.

questions.question: A customs brokerage receives declaration files from thirty carriers, each using its own country codes, date formats and commodity labels. A team now runs every file through a step that normalizes the codes, drops duplicate line items and rejects malformed rows before anything is written to the brokerage's store. Which stage of the data supply chain is that team working in?

options.A: Data collection, the stage that brings the declarations in from the carriers
options.B: Data governance, the stage that decides who may alter a commodity label
options.C: Data activation, with each report mapping the carrier codes as it needs them
options.D: Data processing, the stage that turns raw declarations into a usable form

rationale.correct: Normalizing codes, removing duplicates and rejecting malformed rows is data processing: the stage of the data supply chain that turns what was collected into something later stages can rely on. Data collection has already finished, and data storage, data analysis and data activation all come after.

distractors.A: Data collection is the stage that already completed here, because the declaration files arrived from the carriers before this team touched them.
distractors.B: Deciding who may alter a commodity label is data governance, an ongoing process that runs alongside the whole supply chain instead of occupying a stage in it.
distractors.C: Mapping each carrier's codes inside every report moves the same work to data activation and repeats it for every consumer, leaving the store full of the inconsistencies processing exists to remove.

questions.question: A dental practice group's clinical audit has stalled. Two systems disagree about which patients are due for recall, nobody can say who is permitted to correct a record, and a spreadsheet of decayed contact details has been circulating between practices for a year. The IT manager proposes buying a data quality tool. What does the group need first?

options.A: A data quality tool that finds duplicate and stale patient records in both systems
options.B: A data lake holding both systems' records in native form, so no version is discarded
options.C: A data governance process that sets ownership, access and quality rules for patient data
options.D: Encryption of the patient records at rest, so the circulating spreadsheet cannot be read

rationale.correct: Every failure described is an ownership failure: unowned quality, uncontrolled access, and data nobody is accountable for. A data governance process is what decides who may do what with which data, and without one the group has no basis for saying which recall list is right or who may correct it.

distractors.A: A tool would find the duplicate and stale records and none of the reasons they keep reappearing; with no owner for the recall list, the same defects return after every clean-up.
distractors.B: Landing both systems in native form preserves every version and settles nothing, because the group still cannot say which recall list is authoritative or who may change it.
distractors.D: Encryption protects records from people outside the group's access controls, and this spreadsheet is circulating among staff who are inside them, which is a question of who may hold and share the data.

questions.question: A civil engineering consultancy is choosing a platform for its project data. Each discipline currently keeps its model files in a tool that exports only to its own format, and the partners are determined not to repeat that. Their technology adviser asks which failure modes a commitment to openness and interoperability is meant to prevent. Select the TWO failure modes it addresses.

options.A: Losing access to project data while a regional outage is in progress
options.B: Data silos, where each discipline's information stays trapped inside its own team
options.C: Copies of one model drifting apart as each discipline exports its own version
options.D: Format decay, the recognized term for fidelity lost at every export conversion
options.E: Vendor lock-in, where changing platform means rebuilding or abandoning the data

rationale.correct: Openness and interoperability answer two named failure modes: data silos, which trap value inside a team, and vendor lock-in, which traps it inside a platform. Both are questions about whether information can move, between disciplines and off a supplier's product, which is what open formats and open standards protect.

distractors.A: An outage is an availability problem answered by redundancy and replication, and open formats do not keep a platform serving while a region is down.
distractors.C: Drifting copies are a symptom that silos produce, not the failure mode itself, so naming the symptom leaves the reason each discipline keeps its own copy untouched.
distractors.D: No such named failure mode belongs to this vocabulary. Lossy exports are one way lock-in bites, and the failure mode is the lock-in.

questions.question: A car rental agency is rebuilding its booking ledger. A vehicle must never be double-booked, and one booking service will serve branches in North America, Europe and Asia, all reading and writing the same reservations. The agency wants a relational database it does not have to shard by region. Which Google Cloud product fits?

options.A: BigQuery, so reservation history can be analyzed alongside branch performance
options.B: Bigtable, which scales to very high write volumes across large key ranges
options.C: Spanner, a relational database with globally consistent transactions
options.D: Cloud SQL in one region, with read replicas serving the other two continents

rationale.correct: Two constraints decide this: relational transactions that stay consistent everywhere, and no regional sharding. Spanner is the managed relational product built for globally consistent transactional writes at scale, and a double-booking is exactly the anomaly that global consistency prevents.

distractors.A: BigQuery is the analytics warehouse, so it is where the agency would examine reservation history, not where a booking is written and read back moments later by another branch.
distractors.B: Bigtable serves enormous wide-column write volumes and offers no relational transactions, so nothing in it would stop two branches booking the same vehicle.
distractors.D: Read replicas spread reads across continents while every write still lands in one region, which leaves the agency sharding or accepting distant writes, the outcome the requirement rules out.

questions.question: An auction house is planning storage for three new workloads: bidder account records with fixed fields and enforced links between them, high-resolution lot photographs and condition videos, and a catalog where each lot carries whatever attributes its category needs. Before any product is shortlisted, the architect asks the team to classify all three. Which classification is correct?

options.A: All three are non-relational: only fixed rows and columns count as relational
options.B: Relational for accounts, object storage for the media, non-relational for the catalog
options.C: Relational for accounts and the catalog, with object storage for the media
options.D: Non-relational for accounts and the catalog, with object storage for the media

rationale.correct: Classification comes before product choice. Fixed fields with enforced links are relational and belong to structured query language; photographs and videos are files, which is object storage; a catalog whose attributes vary by category is non-relational, the NoSQL shape. Getting these right is what makes the product shortlist short.

distractors.A: Relational describes an enforced structure of related tables, not a spreadsheet layout, and bidder accounts with fixed fields and enforced links are the textbook relational case.
distractors.C: Treating the catalog as relational forces every category's attributes into one schema, which is the constraint a non-relational model exists to lift; the other two assignments here are right.
distractors.D: Bidder accounts with fixed fields and enforced links are the relational case, so classifying them as non-relational discards the referential integrity the auction house depends on.

questions.question: An architectural design practice keeps every completed project's drawing set in Cloud Storage. Once a building is handed over, its set is opened only if a defect claim arrives, which for any given project happens perhaps once or twice in a decade, yet professional indemnity rules require the practice to keep every set for fifteen years. The sets are large. Which storage class should the handed-over sets use?

options.A: Standard, so the drawings are available the moment a defect claim arrives
options.B: Nearline, the class priced for data that is read about once a month
options.C: Whatever class the practice's other buckets use, to keep billing lines consistent
options.D: Archive, the class priced for data retained for years and rarely read

rationale.correct: Storage class follows access frequency, not data size. Drawing sets opened perhaps once or twice in a decade but kept for fifteen years are retention data, and Archive is priced for exactly that: the lowest storage cost, with a retrieval cost accepted on the rare occasion a claim arrives.

distractors.A: Immediate availability is what Standard is priced for, and it answers the wrong question here, leaving the practice paying hot-data rates every month for sets almost nobody opens.
distractors.B: Nearline is priced for data read about once a month, and these sets are read far less often than that, so the practice would pay a premium the access pattern does not justify.
distractors.C: Matching the other buckets keeps the invoice tidy and ignores the only fact that decides a storage class, which is how often this data is actually read.

questions.question: A bicycle-share operator has just launched in a new city and is putting ride telemetry and docking-station images into Cloud Storage. Nobody can yet say which of it will be read daily and which will go untouched, and the operator expects the pattern to keep shifting as routes settle. A junior analyst offers to review the buckets each quarter and move objects between classes by hand. What should the operator do instead?

options.A: Enable Autoclass so each object moves between classes on its own access pattern
options.B: Run the analyst's review monthly instead of quarterly, so misplaced objects cost less
options.C: Put every bucket in Standard until the access pattern is understood, then revisit
options.D: Put every bucket in Archive, the cheapest storage rate, and accept retrieval costs

rationale.correct: When access patterns are unknown and expected to shift, choosing classes by hand is a guess that has to be repeated forever. Autoclass removes the guess: the platform observes how each object is actually accessed and moves it between classes, so the operator sets a policy once instead of running a review cycle.

distractors.B: A monthly cycle shortens the window in which an object sits in the wrong class and does nothing about nobody being able to predict which objects those are, so the review still runs forever.
distractors.C: Holding everything in Standard until the pattern is understood pays hot-data rates for data that is already going cold, and the operator has said the pattern will keep changing.
distractors.D: The cheapest storage rate is not the cheapest outcome: telemetry that turns out to be read daily would be retrieved from Archive every time, and retrieval is what that class charges for.

questions.question: A commercial laundry service runs its route-scheduling system on a self-managed database server that is three years past its support window. The application vendor will not certify any change to the database engine, and the service employs no developers of its own. The board wants the server out of the basement before winter. Which route should the service take?

options.A: Refactor the scheduling application onto a cloud-native database to lift the vendor constraint
options.B: Retain the server in the basement and revisit once the vendor certifies a change
options.C: Migrate the database as it is onto a managed service running the same engine
options.D: Modernize onto an analytics product so route history can be queried at scale

rationale.correct: The route is decided by what the organization can actually change. A certification that forbids an engine change and the absence of developers rule out modernizing the application, while an unsupported server rules out standing still, which leaves migrating the database as it is onto a managed service running the same engine, where the operational burden transfers and the application sees no difference.

distractors.A: Refactoring is the route for organizations that intend to change the application, and this one may not: the vendor will not certify an engine change, and there are no developers to make it.
distractors.B: Retaining the server keeps an unsupported database in the basement through another winter, and nothing suggests the vendor's position is about to change.
distractors.D: An analytics product answers questions about route history and would not run the scheduling system's transactional workload, which is the workload that has to move.

questions.question: A childcare centre network employs one analyst, and every manager's question about occupancy, staffing ratios or waiting lists becomes a ticket in that analyst's queue. Managers wait days for numbers they needed the same morning, and some have started keeping private spreadsheets. The operations director wants managers answering their own questions from the same governed figures. Which capability delivers that?

options.A: A data warehouse consolidating every centre's records into one queryable store
options.B: Looker, which democratizes access to data by putting governed analysis in managers' hands
options.C: An access review that grants each manager rights to query the underlying tables
options.D: A second analyst, so the queue is served at twice the current rate

rationale.correct: The bottleneck is reach, not storage and not permissions: the numbers already exist, and one person is the only route to them. Looker democratizes access to data, so managers explore governed, consistent figures for themselves and analysis reaches people who are not analysts.

distractors.A: Consolidating every centre's records into one store is worth doing and changes nothing about who can ask a question, so the analyst's queue survives intact.
distractors.C: Granting rights to the underlying tables answers who may read the data, not who can use it, and a manager with table access and no way to interpret it still files a ticket.
distractors.D: Doubling the analyst team halves the wait at best and keeps every question routed through a specialist, which is the arrangement the director wants to end.

questions.question: A driving school franchise runs its business intelligence tool against a nightly extract copied out of BigQuery into a separate reporting database. Branch managers complain that pass-rate dashboards are always a day behind, and that they have to leave the booking system to look at them at all. What does connecting the tool directly to BigQuery buy the franchise?

options.A: Lower storage cost, with the separate reporting database no longer maintained
options.B: Fresher figures, from copying the extract into the reporting database hourly
options.C: Dashboards that refresh on demand, with the booking system left as it is
options.D: Real-time reports and dashboards fed by BigQuery, with analysis inside the booking workflow

rationale.correct: Putting business intelligence on top of the warehouse rather than beside one removes the copy. Real-time reports and dashboards are fed directly by BigQuery, so what a manager sees is the current state, and integrating data into workflows puts the answer where the work already happens instead of in a separate tool.

distractors.A: Retiring the reporting database does save its cost, and cost is not what the managers are describing: they are describing stale numbers and a context switch.
distractors.B: Copying more often narrows the gap and keeps the design that creates it, so between copies the dashboard still shows a snapshot and the manager still leaves the booking system to read it.
distractors.C: On-demand refresh answers the day-behind complaint alone, and the second complaint is that analysis lives outside the workflow, which an unchanged booking system leaves exactly as it was.

questions.question: An elder-care residence operator runs one nightly batch over all of its data and is deciding which of four needs would justify real-time streaming analytics as well. Which need has the shape that a batch window cannot serve?

options.A: A resident's wearable reports a fall, and night staff must be sent to the right room
options.B: Occupancy by wing is set against the same month last year for the trustees' pack
options.C: The nightly batch is rerun hourly so the duty manager sees a fresher picture
options.D: Shift incident reports are summarized for the weekly quality review meeting

rationale.correct: Real-time streaming analytics earns its place where the answer expires. A fall detected at night is worth acting on in the moment and worth nothing in tomorrow's report, and recognizing that shape, a decision whose value decays faster than the batch window, is what separates a streaming need from a reporting need.

distractors.B: Setting occupancy against the same month last year is what a batch is for, and the trustees' pack is prepared on a schedule with nothing in it decaying overnight.
distractors.C: Rerunning the same batch more often shortens the gap and keeps the design, so every hour the duty manager is still reading a snapshot and a fall still waits for the next run.
distractors.D: Shift reports summarized for a weekly meeting describe what already happened, which is how the operator learns about incidents afterwards rather than how staff are directed during one.

questions.question: A facilities management firm has fitted client buildings with meters that emit a reading every few seconds, and three teams, covering alarms, billing and an energy dashboard, each want every reading. The firm needs a layer that accepts readings as they arrive and delivers them to all consumers, without the meters having to know who is listening. Which product performs that job?

options.A: Dataflow, which processes each reading as it passes through the pipeline
options.B: A frequent file export from the meter gateway that each team collects for itself
options.C: Pub/Sub, which ingests the readings and distributes them to every subscriber
options.D: Direct connections from the meter gateway into each of the three teams' systems

rationale.correct: Ingestion and distribution is Pub/Sub's stage of the pipeline: it accepts events as they arrive and delivers them to every subscriber, so publishers and consumers never need to know about each other. Dataflow's stage comes next, processing what has been ingested, and Managed Service for Apache Spark runs Spark workloads, which is a third stage again.

distractors.A: Dataflow processes readings that something else has already ingested, so it is the neighboring stage, and pointing the meters at it leaves nothing decoupling publishers from consumers.
distractors.B: A file export on a schedule holds every reading until the next file and makes each team responsible for fetching it, which is neither ingestion as events arrive nor distribution to subscribers.
distractors.D: Wiring the gateway into each team's system makes the meters aware of every consumer, so adding a fourth team means changing the gateway, the coupling the firm asked to avoid.

questions.question: A ferry and port operator's board is reviewing two projects. One trains a model on ten years of sailing records so it can predict which crossings will be cancelled; the other drafts passenger notices in three languages from a short prompt. A director asks how the two relate to each other in the field's vocabulary. Which statement is correct?

options.A: Both are generative AI, as each produces an output the operator did not have before
options.B: Both are artificial intelligence: the first is machine learning, the second is generative AI
options.C: Neither is machine learning, which by definition needs labeled data the operator lacks
options.D: The first is machine learning, and so is the second, as a trained model produced it

rationale.correct: The terms nest. Artificial intelligence is the field; machine learning is the subset that learns patterns from data, which is what a cancellation predictor does; and generative AI is the newer branch that produces novel content, which is what a notice drafter does. Naming the level correctly is what stops a board discussion confusing a prediction with a piece of writing.

distractors.A: A cancellation prediction is a value drawn from historical patterns, not novel content, so calling both projects generative AI stretches the newer branch over work it does not describe.
distractors.C: Machine learning covers far more than labeled training data, and a predictor built on ten years of sailing records is the plainest example of it.
distractors.D: Generative AI is indeed built with machine learning, and stopping there leaves the board without the term for the branch that produces content it has never seen before.

questions.question: A flower delivery network's marketing lead says the team uses AI for everything. In practice the team does two things: it runs a dashboard that explains why margins fell over the peak gifting week, and it runs a tool that writes a fresh product description for every new bouquet. The finance director asks which of the two is generative AI. What is the accurate answer?

options.A: Both: a dashboard also produces an explanation the team did not previously have
options.B: The dashboard, where explaining why margins fell means generating an account of them
options.C: Neither: both run on models the network licenses rather than trains for itself
options.D: The description writer, which produces content that did not exist before

rationale.correct: Data analytics and business intelligence describe and explain what already happened, and a margin dashboard is an account of past sales however sophisticated it looks. Generative AI produces content that did not exist, which is what writing a fresh product description is. The line is not how clever the tool looks; it is whether the output is new content or an explanation of existing records.

distractors.A: A dashboard assembles and explains figures the network already holds, and presenting them in a new arrangement is business intelligence rather than the creation of new content.
distractors.B: Explaining why margins fell is exactly the job of data analytics, and describing a cause found in the data is not the same as producing content that was not there.
distractors.C: Whether a model is licensed or trained in-house says nothing about what it does, and both tools keep their categories under either arrangement.

questions.question: A furniture manufacturer has deployed one agentic AI capability. Given a complaint about a delayed order, it checks stock, reschedules the delivery, issues a goodwill credit and confirms all three back to the customer, with no person touching the case. The transformation report records each capability against the function whose work it changes. Which function does this one belong to?

options.A: Customer support, where cases are resolved end to end instead of routed to a person
options.B: Workforce productivity, where staff finish routine work faster with assistance
options.C: Operations, where the scheduling and stock systems are the ones being changed
options.D: Sales experiences, where the goodwill credit is an offer made to retain a customer

rationale.correct: Agentic AI is recorded against the function whose work changes. Here a customer support case is resolved end to end, checked, rescheduled, credited and confirmed, with no handoff to a person at any point. Workforce productivity, sales experiences, product innovation, operations and research are the other functions the same technology transforms, each in a different way.

distractors.B: Workforce productivity is where a person still does the work and finishes it sooner, and here nobody touches the case at all, which is a different kind of change.
distractors.C: The scheduling and stock systems are consulted rather than changed, and operations would be the answer if the agent were reshaping how production or logistics run.
distractors.D: The goodwill credit is one step inside the resolution, so picking it out records a fragment of the case instead of the function whose work the agent now performs.

questions.question: A home renovation marketplace employs no data scientists and needs an AI-powered helpdesk assistant answering customers before its spring campaign opens. Its chief executive has read Google's list of AI advantages and asks which one speaks to the marketplace's situation. Which advantage does?

options.A: Sophisticated first-party models, developed by Google rather than licensed in
options.B: The best infrastructure for AI, so the assistant serves its answers quickly
options.C: Pre-built AI agents and applications, adopted without building a model
options.D: An all-in-one AI developer platform, on which the marketplace builds the assistant

rationale.correct: Each claimed advantage answers a different question, and the question here is how an organization with no data scientists gets a capability live before a campaign. Pre-built AI agents and applications is the claim that answers it, because the capability is adopted rather than built. Sophisticated models, the best infrastructure for AI and the all-in-one AI developer platform all matter to organizations that are building.

distractors.A: Model quality is a real advantage, and it answers what an assistant could do rather than how a marketplace with no data scientists gets one running before the campaign.
distractors.B: Infrastructure strength shows up in how fast and how cheaply a model serves, which is a question the marketplace has not asked and could not act on either way.
distractors.D: The developer platform is the route for teams that intend to build, and this marketplace has nobody to build with, so choosing it adds work the deadline cannot absorb.

keywords: deriving business insights from large datasets
questions.question: A hospitality staffing agency is shortlisting candidate problems for its first machine learning project, and its head of operations wants only the ones machine learning is genuinely the right tool for. Select the TWO problems that qualify.

options.A: A shift-matching rulebook grown to hundreds of conditions that nobody can maintain
options.B: Choosing which of two payroll providers offers the agency better contract terms
options.C: Retaining five years of timesheet history instead of deleting it after one year
options.D: Forecasting which of thousands of weekly postings will go unfilled, one by one
options.E: Sending each worker the confirmation email for a shift they have just accepted

rationale.correct: Machine learning earns its place in two of these: replacing or simplifying rule-based systems, where a rulebook has grown past what anyone can maintain, and scaling business decisions, where a judgment must be made thousands of times over and no team can make each one by hand. The third problem it suits, deriving business insights from large datasets, is not on this shortlist.

distractors.B: Choosing between two suppliers is a commercial negotiation with a handful of variables and no pattern to learn, so it is settled by reading the terms.
distractors.C: Keeping more history is a genuine prerequisite for training anything, and it is data management rather than the business problem a model would solve.
distractors.E: Sending a confirmation when a shift is accepted is deterministic automation: the rule is one line, there is nothing to learn, and calling it machine learning stretches the term.

questions.question: An independent record label's royalty run keeps failing reconciliation. Investigation shows that one recording is listed four times under slightly different spellings of its title, so each quarter's payment is split across the four entries and none of them matches the contract. Which dimension of data quality does that defect violate?

options.A: Consistency, where two records of the same thing disagree with one another
options.B: Uniqueness would be broken only if the duplicates were identical rather than spelled differently
options.C: Timeliness, where the duplicates accumulated over several years of catalog entry
options.D: Uniqueness, where one real-world thing is recorded more than once

rationale.correct: Uniqueness is the dimension that says one real-world entity should appear once. Four entries for one recording break it, which is why the royalty run splits a payment that should have been whole. Completeness, timeliness, validity, accuracy and consistency each name a different defect, and none of them describes a thing recorded more than once.

distractors.A: Consistency covers records that contradict each other, such as two royalty rates for one contract, and these entries do not disagree about anything; there are simply too many of them.
distractors.B: Duplicates rarely arrive identical, and near-identical spellings of one title are exactly the case uniqueness exists to catch.
distractors.C: How long the duplicates took to accumulate is true and beside the point, as timeliness is about data being current and these entries are wrong the day they are created.

questions.question: An industrial bakery has built a model that scores supplier batches on arrival and rejects the poorest. In trial it graded more reliably than the quality team. When a supplier disputed a rejection, nobody at the bakery could say which properties of that batch drove its score. The commercial director wants to go live next month on the strength of the trial. What should the bakery recognize?

options.A: The trial settles it: a model that grades more reliably than the quality team has earned deployment
options.B: A decision the bakery cannot explain is a decision it cannot defend, which blocks going live
options.C: A notice should be published telling suppliers that rejections are scored by a model
options.D: The quality team should review each rejection afterwards and reverse the ones that look wrong

rationale.correct: Explainability is a condition of deployment, not a refinement after it. A rejection the bakery cannot explain is a rejection it cannot defend to the supplier who disputes it, and explainable and responsible AI is what makes the decision reviewable at all. Strong trial results describe how often the model is right and say nothing about whether its reasoning can be shown.

distractors.A: Grading more reliably is the usual reason to adopt a model and is not sufficient here, as the constraint the dispute exposed is whether a rejection can be explained.
distractors.C: Telling suppliers that a model made the decision is honest and leaves the dispute where it was, given that the bakery still cannot say why this batch was rejected.
distractors.D: Reviewing rejections afterwards catches errors after a supplier has already been refused, and the reviewers face the same unexplainable score the disputing supplier did.

questions.question: A language school network's innovation group brings four generative AI proposals to its ethics review, and every one is technically feasible with the tools the network already licenses. The review is asked to identify the proposal that responsible use rules out. Which proposal should it refuse?

options.A: Publishing thousands of machine-written course reviews under invented student names
options.B: Drafting lesson plans that a teacher reviews and signs before any class uses them
options.C: Generating practice dialogues at a volume no human author could write by hand
options.D: Scoring student essays, with marks released only after a tutor confirms each one

rationale.correct: Responsible use is a legitimacy judgment, not a feasibility one. Reviews attributed to students who do not exist produce volume with no accountable business purpose and deceive the readers they are aimed at, which is what explainable and responsible AI rules out. Every other proposal has a named purpose and a person who answers for the output.

distractors.B: A teacher who reviews and signs a lesson plan is the accountable owner of it, which is the arrangement responsible use asks for rather than the one it forbids.
distractors.C: Producing more material than a human author could write describes scale, and scale is not what makes a use illegitimate; practice dialogues have an obvious teaching purpose.
distractors.D: A tutor confirming each mark before release keeps a person accountable for every decision that reaches a student, so the safeguard the review looks for is present.

questions.question: A microfinance lender wants an AI capability that competitors cannot simply buy: its own loan-performance history is the asset, and the board says the capability must be built on it. The lender employs two experienced data scientists and has set no launch date. Which factor should dominate its choice of AI approach?

options.A: Implementation speed, so a capability reaches the field as early as possible
options.B: Technical expertise requirements, keeping the approach inside a small team's reach
options.C: Potential for business differentiation, which the lender's own history can buy
options.D: Development effort, taking whichever approach is cheapest to build and run

rationale.correct: Approach selection turns on the constraint that actually binds. Here it is potential for business differentiation: the lender's own loan-performance history is the asset a competitor cannot copy, and only an approach that builds on it converts that into an advantage. Implementation speed, development effort, technical expertise requirements and choice and flexibility are the other factors, and none of them is under pressure in this situation.

distractors.A: Implementation speed matters where a date binds, and the board has set none, so optimizing for it would trade away the differentiation the lender said it wants.
distractors.B: Expertise is a real constraint for organizations without specialists, and this lender has two experienced data scientists, so the approaches that need them are open to it.
distractors.D: Taking the cheapest thing to build is a budget instinct rather than a selection factor, and it points at exactly the generic capability a competitor could buy tomorrow.

questions.question: A minor-league sports franchise now runs four AI agents built separately by its ticketing, merchandising and community teams. Nobody can say what data each agent may reach, two teams have built the same lookup twice, and no one approved any of them. The chief operating officer wants one place to build, deploy and govern all agents. Which Google Cloud offering is that?

options.A: Gemini, the general-purpose model the three teams are already calling
options.B: Looker, so every team reports from one governed set of figures
options.C: Agent Registry, the catalog where deployed agents are listed and approved
options.D: The Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform, for building, deploying and governing agents

rationale.correct: What the franchise needs is not another model or another report; it is one place where agents are built, deployed and governed across the organization. That is what the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform is for in business terms, and it is what turns duplicated agents and unclear data access from a per-team accident into something visible and manageable.

distractors.A: Gemini is the model an agent calls, which is exactly what the three teams already do; a model supplies capability, not a place to govern what is built with it.
distractors.B: Governed reporting puts every team on the same figures and says nothing about which agents exist, what each may reach, or who approved them.
distractors.C: No Google Cloud offering carries that name, and a catalog alone would list the problem rather than provide the build-and-deploy surface the officer asked for.

questions.question: A museum and heritage trust holds three thousand hours of recorded oral-history interviews on tape. Researchers can currently find a passage only by listening through a recording, so the trust wants the spoken words available as searchable text. It employs no machine learning staff. Which Google Cloud offering should the trust use?

options.A: The Speech-to-Text API, which converts recorded audio into text
options.B: The Cloud Translation API, which converts text between language pairs
options.C: AutoML on Agent Platform, training a transcription model on the tapes
options.D: Cloud Storage for the tapes, so researchers can stream any recording in full

rationale.correct: Matching the modality to a solved task is the judgment here: audio to the Speech-to-Text API, images to the Vision API, language pairs to the Cloud Translation API. The trust needs spoken words as text and has no machine learning staff, so a pre-trained API that already performs the task is the route, and building anything would repeat finished work.

distractors.B: The Cloud Translation API moves text between languages and needs text to start from, which is precisely what the trust does not yet have.
distractors.C: Training a transcription model reproduces a solved task, and the trust has nobody to train, evaluate or maintain it.
distractors.D: Storing the tapes makes them playable and not searchable, so a researcher still listens through recordings to find the passage they want.

questions.question: A natural-gas distributor wants its engineers' typed field notes turned into incident summaries: each note must be read, a probable cause inferred, a severity suggested and a plain-language summary drafted for the regulator. The distributor wants all of that called from its own back-office system. Which route fits the job?

options.A: The Vision API, which extracts information from documents and images
options.B: Gemini through the Agent Platform API, which handles broad generative work
options.C: The Cloud Translation API, so summaries reach the regulator in its language
options.D: A classification model trained on past notes to predict a severity band

rationale.correct: The job needs broad generative capability over free text: reading, inferring, judging and drafting in one pass. Gemini is the general-purpose model for that, and the Agent Platform API is the programmatic route to it from the distributor's own back-office system. A single-task perception API answers one modality-specific question and none of these four.

distractors.A: The Vision API is for images and scanned pages, and these notes are already typed text, so extraction is not the problem left to solve.
distractors.C: Translation is a real need if the regulator reads another language, and it operates on a summary that something else must first infer and draft.
distractors.D: A severity classifier delivers one of the four outputs and leaves the reading, the inferred cause and the drafted summary undone.

questions.question: An office furniture rental firm holds ten years of its own inspection photographs, each labeled with the damage grade an assessor gave it, and wants new photographs graded the same way. The work would be done by two business analysts who are comfortable with data and have never trained a model. Which route fits both the data and the expertise?

options.A: Agent Studio on Agent Platform, assembling an agent over the photograph library
options.B: The Vision API, which recognizes objects and text in images out of the box
options.C: Hiring a machine learning engineer to build a custom model from scratch
options.D: AutoML on Agent Platform, training a custom model on the labeled photographs

rationale.correct: Two facts decide the route: the firm has its own labeled data, and nobody on the team has trained a model. AutoML on Agent Platform is built for that pair, training a custom model on your own data without deep machine learning skills, while Agent Studio on Agent Platform is the low-code route when the job is assembling an agent rather than training a model.

distractors.A: Assembling an agent is the low-code route to orchestrating tasks, and this firm's problem is a grading model trained on its own labeled photographs.
distractors.B: A pre-trained vision service recognizes general objects and text, and it has never seen this firm's grading scale, so it cannot reproduce an assessor's grade.
distractors.C: Hiring a specialist to build from scratch is real capability and more machinery than the situation needs, given that a managed training service covers the same ground with the team the firm already has.

questions.question: An orchard and packhouse cooperative is presenting the infrastructure section of its AI business case to its members, who are growers. They want to know what the cooperative is buying when the paper says AI infrastructure, and why it is not simply a bigger machine. Which description states what that layer is?

options.A: A private cloud region reserved for the cooperative's own AI workloads
options.B: A managed warehouse keeping the cooperative's harvest data ready for training
options.C: AI Hypercomputer, integrating GPUs and TPUs with leading software and open standards
options.D: A fixed annual allocation of accelerator hours bought before the season starts

rationale.correct: The AI infrastructure layer is the compute that models are trained and served on. AI Hypercomputer integrates GPUs and TPUs with industry-leading software and open standards, so what the cooperative buys is an integrated stack rather than loose hardware, and its cost is controlled through flexible consumption models, which is what lets a seasonal business pay for accelerators in the weeks it uses them.

distractors.A: A reserved private region describes where capacity sits and who else may use it, which is a deployment model rather than the accelerator layer the paper is naming.
distractors.B: Keeping harvest data ready for training is the data platform's job, and the growers are asking about the layer that the training itself runs on.
distractors.D: Buying a fixed allocation in advance is one way to pay for accelerators, and paying for them is not what the layer is; flexible consumption is what keeps a seasonal business from buying capacity it will not use.

questions.question: An outdoor advertising operator holds every campaign's impression and pricing history in BigQuery, and its three analysts are fluent in SQL and in nothing else. They want to predict which advertising sites will go unsold next quarter. The data team will not allow the warehouse to be copied into a separate environment. What should the operator use?

options.A: BigQuery ML, which trains and serves models from standard SQL queries
options.B: AutoML on Agent Platform, after exporting the campaign history to it
options.C: Looker, which would chart unsold inventory by site and by quarter
options.D: A weekly report of last quarter's unsold sites, compiled by the analysts

rationale.correct: Two constraints point the same way: the analysts speak standard SQL, and the data may not leave the warehouse. BigQuery ML trains and serves models with standard SQL queries where the data already lives, so the prediction is built by the people who already query it and nothing is copied anywhere.

distractors.B: Exporting the campaign history into a separate training environment is exactly the copy the data team refuses, and it moves the work somewhere the analysts do not work.
distractors.C: Charting unsold inventory shows what has already happened by site and by quarter, and the operator asked which sites will go unsold next.
distractors.D: A report of last quarter's unsold sites records the outcome after the fact, which arrives far too late to change what a seller does about next quarter.
